output.name: Kessa
output.myth: On the longest day, when the Lamp Road burns brightest over the cliffs, Kessa was flown by her aunt from the ledge at Haskel's Point. She was made of old sail and goat gut, and her tail was long enough to hold a child's whole summer. A grey hen with a torn foot came down the sky and bit the line through. Tavo laughed and let the kite go. The string went on up to Aun, who is careless with other people's rope. Kessa went the other way, along the road. The Ferry Sail hangs south-west of her, the Southing Goose east, and neither will take her hand. Hesk has counted her every night since, from the Tally Kite, and the count is always one short of a full reel. Her aunt still stands on the ledge at midsummer with an empty hand held up. Kessa is looking for that hand. If you see a kite on the Lamp Road with a knot at its tail and no string beneath, do not wave. Keep your own line tight, and feed the gulls nothing.
output.finding: From the Ferry Sail, look about one fist north-east along the Lamp Road, and Kessa is hanging there.
